# Bukayo Saka | From Ealing to the World

> An immersive digital tribute to Bukayo Saka — Arsenal's No.7, England international, FA Cup winner, and one of football's brightest talents. Born in Ealing, London on 5 September 2001, Saka rose from the Hale End Academy to the top of world football.

## Player Overview

- **Full Name:** Bukayo Ayoyinka Saka
- **Known As:** "Little Chilli"
- **Date of Birth:** 5 September 2001
- **Place of Birth:** Ealing, London, England
- **Nationality:** English (Nigerian heritage)
- **Position:** Winger / Right-winger
- **Current Club:** Arsenal F.C. (academy 2008 — present, professional debut 2018)
- **Shirt Number:** 7 (Arsenal)
- **International Team:** England senior squad (debut October 2020)

## Career Statistics

Statistics on this site update automatically from live football APIs (FPL, football-data.org) with 1–6 hour caching. Career baseline through end of 2023/24:

- **Premier League Goals:** 50+ (career)
- **Premier League Assists:** 64+ (career)
- **Arsenal Total Goals:** 83+ (all competitions)
- **Arsenal Total Assists:** 64+
- **Premier League Goal Involvements:** 147+
- **England Caps:** 63+
- **England Goals:** 16+
- **England Assists:** 17+

## Career Timeline

### 2008 — Hale End Academy
Joined Arsenal's youth academy in Ealing aged seven. Progressed through every age group without leaving the club.

### 2018 — Professional Debut
Made his first-team debut in the UEFA Europa League on 29 November 2018 at age 17, becoming one of Arsenal's youngest debutants.

### 2019 — First Premier League Appearance
Broke into the first-team squad under Unai Emery and later flourished under Mikel Arteta.

### 2020 — England Call-Up
Called into the England senior squad for the first time in October 2020, aged 19. Provided an assist on his international debut.

### 2021 — Arsenal No.7
Permanently awarded Arsenal's iconic No.7 shirt — previously worn by club legends.

### 2021 — Euro 2020 (held 2021)
Featured in England's run to the final at Wembley. Missed his penalty in the shootout against Italy — the weight of a nation — before bouncing back as one of England's most trusted players.

### 2022 — World Cup, Qatar
One of England's standout performers in the group stage and knockout rounds. Scored and assisted throughout the tournament.

### 2023 — England Men's Player of the Year
Won the FA's England Men's Player of the Year award, voted for by supporters.

### 2024 — FA Cup Winner
Won the FA Cup with Arsenal, ending a 14-year wait for the club. Saka was central to Arsenal's run throughout the competition.

### 2024 — Euro 2024
Reached the final in Berlin against Spain. Featured prominently throughout the tournament as one of the Three Lions' most important players.

## Beyond the Pitch

### Big Shoe Foundation
Saka's personal charitable initiative that provides shoes and educational support to children in Nigeria, helping those in need in his family's homeland.

### Ealing Community
Deeply committed to his home borough of Ealing, West London. Has supported local community projects and youth programmes.

### Commercial Partnerships
- **Nike** — Long-term partnership including signature Mercurial Furon boot collaborations
- **Nando's** — Brand ambassador; a well-known fan of the restaurant chain
- **EA Sports** — Featured prominently in FIFA/EA FC
- Additional partnerships with global brands in fashion and lifestyle

## Site Sections

1. **Hero** — Full-screen cinematic introduction
2. **THE STORY** — Animated signature reveal leading into his life story; scroll-driven
3. **Hale End Academy** — Horizontal scroll gallery through his youth career
4. **Professional Debut** — Scroll sequence: Arsenal debut → FA Cup → England call-up → first England goal
5. **Number 7** — Receiving the iconic Arsenal shirt
6. **Club & Country** — Dual immersive narratives: Arsenal ("The Gunner") and England ("The Lion")
7. **England Story** — 3D depth-scrolling journey through international career chapters: International Debut, World Cup 2022, Player of the Year, Euro 2024
8. **Beyond the Pitch** — Charity, community, and commercial life
9. **Match Center** — Live fixture widget with upcoming Arsenal matches and current season stats
10. **Footer** — Contact and social media links

## Live Data Sources

- **Current season stats:** Fantasy Premier League (FPL) public API — updates within 6 hours of each match
- **Fixtures:** football-data.org, api-football (RapidAPI), TheSportsDB — cascading fallbacks
- **Career baseline:** Manually maintained in codebase, updated at start of each season

## Technical Stack

- Next.js 16 (App Router) with Turbopack
- React 19, Framer Motion 12, Tailwind CSS v4
- Lenis smooth scroll
- CSS 3D perspective transforms for immersive scenes
- Next.js ISR for cached API responses
